newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end with slight rise.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end with slight rise.

text.p: French shares showed their resilience, closing with a narrow gain despite a weaker tone on Wall Street.
Traders said buying at the start of the February account and continued strength of the dollar supported the Paris market.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 4.83 points or 0.2 percent at 2,435.17, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,436 from 2,429 on Friday's close.

* Suez rose 3.07 percent to 231.90 francs as the market welcomed its sale of a four billion franc property loan portfolio which will mean taking a one-billion franc charge on 1996 accounts and giving a net result of 800 million.
* Rhone-Poulenc gains 4.71 percent to 184.60 francs, helped by results of its Rorer pharmaceuticals unit which were at the upper end of forecasts.
* Michelin, rises 1.6 percent to 311.50 francs, helped by a Merrill Lynch upgrade.
* Renault pleases, up 1.65 percent at 117.20, as it confirms it looking for a British supplier to cut costs.

* Societe Generale unchanged at 620 francs but very busy with 913,000 shares traded. Goldman Sachs said in a note that it remained underweight on the bank sector in view of the mediocre performance but does exclude the possibility of a restructuring aong the players.
* CCF fell 2.3 percent to 251 francs as SGE Delahaye downgraded the bank to neutral from outperform, on a view the stock is now fully valued.
* Lyonnaise des Eaux gains 3.48 percent to 535 in arbitrage against Cie Generale des Eaux, down 1.32 percent at 672. -- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
